description:
FILED s473p (Opus, 2026-09-07, on the resume) while running the round's owed
emission A/B bar.

`tools/emission-ab.pl --out DIR` produces a WRONG verdict when DIR is
RELATIVE, and it is the shape a caller reaches for first (`--out
scratch/<label>/ab-out`).

REPRODUCER, on any tree with a git ref to compare against:

    tools/emission-ab.pl --ref <REF> --out scratch/x lib/Config.pm
      sh: 1: cannot create scratch/x/A/0.lisp: Directory nonexistent
      emission-ab: files=1 SAME=0 DIFF=1 RCDIFF=1
    tools/emission-ab.pl --ref <REF> --out $PWD/scratch/x lib/Config.pm
      emission-ab: files=1 SAME=0 DIFF=1 RCDIFF=0        (the honest answer)

THE CAUSE, one line.  The tool sets `$tmp = $out` and then puts side A's
worktree INSIDE it (`$tmp/ref-tree`), and each pair is transpiled by

    system("cd \Q$dir_a\E && ... ./pl2cl < FILE > \Q$ta\E ...")

so side A's output path is resolved relative to the WORKTREE, not to the
caller's cwd.  With the default (a `tempdir(TMPDIR => 1)`) the path is
absolute and the bug cannot fire; only `--out` can be relative.  Side B is
unaffected because its `cd` target is the repo root itself.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT SILENT-WRONG-BY-LUCK: side A produces NO
file, so every pair reads DIFF and every rc reads `A= B=0`.  The run announces
`cannot create ... Directory nonexistent` on stderr, and RCDIFF is non-zero,
which is the signal a reader is told to treat as a hard failure -- so the
verdict is loud rather than silent.  But it is loud in the WRONG direction: a
reader who is chasing DIFFs sees three-of-three DIFF and can spend the time
before noticing the rc column, which is what happened here.

THE FIX is `$out = File::Spec->rel2abs($out) if defined $out;` at option
parse time (or `abs_path`), beside the `@files` absolutisation the script
already does one line later -- it maps its INPUTS through `abs_path` and not
its output dir.  Optionally also refuse an `--out` that is inside the repo
tree, since the worktree add would then nest a worktree under the checkout.

NOT FIXED HERE: the resume brief's scope was the owed bars, and this is a
tools-only bug with an immediate workaround (pass an absolute path).  It is
in scope for the next session that touches `tools/`.
subject: tools/emission-ab.pl --out with a RELATIVE path makes side A write nothing, so every pair reads DIFF (the output dir is resolved inside the ref worktree)
